c.tagline: Pyrenean capital of duty-free shopping and thermal spas.

taxi.fareNote: Government-regulated fixed tariffs by zone/destination rather than a running meter; confirm the price with the driver before departure.

emergency.note: 112 also reaches all emergency services as the general European number.

hood_desc: Andorra la Vella's medieval core with cobbled lanes, the historic Casa de la Vall parliament building and small squares; best for culture lovers who want to walk everywhere.
The country's central shopping boulevard lined with duty-free electronics, fashion and perfume shops; suits shopping-focused visitors who want to be steps from the action.
A lively spa town built around the Caldea thermal complex, with casinos, bars and restaurants; ideal for wellness travelers and those wanting a livelier evening scene.
A quieter, more residential district on the southern edge of town near the road to Spain, with easy driving access; good for families and road-trippers wanting value and space.
A modern business and convention district with larger hotels and easy parking; suits business travelers and those attending events at the nearby congress center.

water.note: Sourced from clean Pyrenees mountain water and safe to drink from the tap.

transit.pay: Andorra la Vella's urban buses are free of charge for everyone, no ticket needed. National intercity coaches connecting parishes charge a small cash or card fare paid to the driver; some routes accept the CoopBus prepaid card.
transit.hours: Urban buses run roughly 7am-9pm on frequent intervals; no true night service, though some lines run later on weekends.
transit.note: The compact city center is very walkable; buses mainly matter for reaching Escaldes-Engordany, ski resorts and other parishes.

air: Andorra–La Seu d'Urgell Airport (LEU, limited service)
train: No railway in Andorra; nearest stations are L'Hospitalet-près-l'Andorre (France) and Barcelona/Lleida (Spain), reached by connecting bus

airport.name: Barcelona–El Prat Airport (BCN)
airport.drive: ~2.5-3 hours by car (mountain roads via Spain)

transit.m: Direct coach/shuttle bus (Nice Car, Alsa, DirectBus) ~3 hr
Train to Lleida + connecting bus ~3.5 hr

tip.r: Not obligatory; rounding up or leaving 5-10% for good service in restaurants is appreciated but not expected.

landmarks: Casa de la Vall
Andorra's former parliament house, a 16th-century stone manor turned seat of government, is the country's most important historic and political landmark.
Santuari de Meritxell
The modern national shrine dedicated to Andorra's patron saint features striking pink-hued architecture by Ricardo Bofill amid a scenic mountainside setting.
Caldea
This futuristic glass thermal spa complex, with its iconic crystalline tower, draws visitors to soak in geothermal waters framed by Pyrenean peaks.
Pont de Paris
A charming stone footbridge over the Gran Valira river, this romantic crossing is a favorite spot for photographing Andorra la Vella's old town.
Església de Sant Esteve
This Romanesque parish church, with its square bell tower, anchors Andorra la Vella's historic quarter and is one of the capital's oldest buildings.
Madriu-Perafita-Claror Valley
This UNESCO World Heritage glacial valley showcases pristine Pyrenean wilderness, stone refuges, and centuries of traditional mountain land use just outside the capital.
Grandvalira Ski Resort
The largest ski area in the Pyrenees offers sweeping snow-capped slopes and panoramic mountain vistas that define Andorra's alpine, adventure-sport identity.
Vallnord (Ordino-Arcalís)
A picturesque ski and mountain-biking resort in the northern valleys, prized for its dramatic granite peaks and uncrowded alpine scenery.
Naturlandia
This mountain adventure park is famous for the Tobotronc, the world's longest alpine coaster, winding thrillingly through dense Pyrenean forest.
Plaça del Poble
Andorra la Vella's central plaza and rooftop park hosts festivals and offers a lively public gathering space with sweeping views over the capital.

train.note: Andorra has no railway at all. The nearest stations are L'Hospitalet-pres-l'Andorre in France (SNCF trains from Toulouse plus the Paris Intercites de Nuit sleeper, with a connecting bus into Andorra) and Barcelona or Lleida in Spain - most travellers simply take a direct coach.

bus.note: Coaches arrive at the Andorra la Vella national bus station (Estacio Nacional d'Autobusos). Andorra is outside the EU/Schengen - carry your passport, as checks happen at both the French and Spanish borders.

ferry.note: Andorra is a landlocked mountain country with no boat services of any kind; the nearest port is Barcelona.

half.name: Vall de Sorteny Natural Park
half.blurb: A glacial valley and botanical refuge with alpine meadows and hundreds of wildflower species.

half.name: Ordino Arcalis and Coma del Forat
half.blurb: Andorra's wild northern valley, prized for cirque lakes and dramatic high-mountain scenery.

half.name: La Seu d'Urgell
half.blurb: A charming Spanish border town with a fine 12th-century Romanesque cathedral and old quarter.

half.name: Ax-les-Thermes
half.blurb: A pretty French spa town where visitors soak in natural thermal springs among the mountains.

half.name: Engolasters Lake
half.blurb: A serene mountain lake ringed by pine forest, popular for easy walks and photos.
